titulo: Deliver: slides, dashboards, and shared documents
lead: Finished work only matters when it reaches someone. Now you can ask Claude for a presentation, graphic, numbers dashboard, or document, see it finished in the conversation, make changes in plain language, and share it by link. In this lesson, Carla turns lesson 1 into 7 slides and creates a guest document the team can edit together, checking it before sending.
objetivo: Turn the work into slides, a dashboard, or a shared document, and check it before sending.

aprende.t: The deliverable types and which plan supports each one
Adjust the piece with words, without another program
Check 3 numbers or dates before sharing
Share with view, comment, or edit access

hero_alt: Teacher’s desk: a laptop showing a black-and-yellow presentation about spreadsheets, next to a cup and a notebook with three circled numbers.

secoes.sub: Tap or click each step. Check it before sharing the link, never after.

nos.detalhe: Say what you want, where the content comes from, and what it should look like: how many slides, what colors, who will read it. The clearer your request, the fewer back-and-forths later.
The piece appears right in the conversation, without opening another program. Look at it as your student or client will: can they understand it in a few seconds?
You make changes by saying things like: "make the text bigger," "remove slide 4," "replace the chart with a table." One change at a time is easier to check.

Choose 3 numbers or dates in the piece and compare them with the original source: the spreadsheet, calendar, or script. Claude can get a number wrong with complete confidence. If one of the three is wrong, check them all.

The piece starts out private: only you can see it. In the Share button, you choose who can access it. In a document, each person can view, comment, or edit. As the doc owner, you can tag @Claude in a comment so it can review the document right there.

secoes.legenda: Asking, viewing, and adjusting can take a few rounds. Checking and sharing happen once, in that order.

rolagem_fim.texto: Describe the piece in words, adjust it in words, check 3 numbers against the source, and only then share the link.

secoes.sub: The official names and which plans include each one. There is no "Motion Studio": the correct name is Claude Motion.

texto: Claude Slides makes presentations; Claude Design makes graphics, like a post cover or a poster.
Both are available on all plans. They’re the best place to start.

exemplo.texto: 7 slides for lesson 1 and a graphic to promote the lesson in the channel.

texto: A dashboard is a panel of numbers: charts and totals on one screen, built from a spreadsheet or data you provide.
It’s in beta (testing). Before showing it to anyone, check 3 numbers against the source.

exemplo.texto: A dashboard showing course sign-ups by month, built from her spreadsheet.

texto: Claude Motion creates animated videos with code and exports them as MP4 files.
It’s in beta and available only on Team and Enterprise plans. It doesn’t appear on Pro, Max, or Ultra, so stick with Slides and Design.
Claude creates a document you can share by link. Everyone works on the same copy, with no versions lost in email.
Anyone who opens it needs to sign in with a Claude account. You choose who can view, comment, or edit.

exemplo.texto: A list of guests for this month’s livestreams, updated by the moderator.

secoes.titulo: Carla’s prompts: slides, dashboard, and artwork
secoes.sub: Works on claude.ai and in the app. Send the script with your request or mention the file if you’re in the Code tab; replace spreadsheet-course/… with the path to your file (.md, Word, or PDF; see lesson 2).

blocos.conteudo:
Create a 7-slide presentation from the lesson 1 script (spreadsheet-course/lesson-1/script.md).
Audience: adults who have never used formulas.
One idea per slide, no more than 20 words per slide, large text.
Colors: black and yellow.
Slide 7: an exercise for the student to do on their own.

Slide 3: replace the text with a spreadsheet example with 4 rows.
Slide 5: larger text and fewer words.
Don’t change the other slides.

List all numbers, dates, and formulas that appear in the 7 slides.
For each one, say which line of the script it’s on.
Mark anything that isn’t in the script with ATTENTION.

Create a dashboard from this spreadsheet: <attach the spreadsheet or give the file name>.
Show subscribers by month in a chart and highlight the period total.
Use only the numbers in the spreadsheet. Don’t make any up.

Create a square image to promote <what you want to promote> on my channel.
Short title, large text, black and yellow colors.
No more than 12 words in the image.

abas.html:
1. A spreadsheet isn’t rocket science.
  2. Cell, row, and column: the address of everything.
  3. A shopping list with 4 items.
  4. The first formula: =SUM(B2:B5).
  5. When the sum is wrong: a cell with text.
  6. Copy the formula down.
  7. Exercise: add up the week’s expenses.

• =SUM(B2:B5) (slide 4): script, line 18.
  • 4 items (slide 3): script, line 12.
  • ATTENTION: "7 days" (slide 7): it isn’t in the script; I added it. Want to keep it?

• Ask for everything again because of one slide: request an edit to just that slide.
  • Send it without checking the numbers: a pretty slide with the wrong formula makes for a wrong lesson.

secoes.sub: A Claude Doc the team can edit together.

blocos.conteudo:
Create a document to track guests for my community’s livestreams in December.
A table with: name, livestream topic, date, time, and status (invited, confirmed, recorded).
Start with 3 sample rows marked EXAMPLE.
Below the table, add a short list of what to do during the week of the live stream.
Make it ready to share with my assistant.

abas.html:
1. Click Share on the document.
  2. Choose access, for example Only you or Anyone with the link, plus an email invitation. Options vary by plan.
  3. For your assistant: send an email invitation with edit permission.
  4. Test it: send the link to someone on your team and ask them to open it. They’ll sign in with their Claude account.

Carla, the doc owner, comments on a livestream row:

"@Claude, check whether any date falls on a December holiday and let me know here."

Claude replies in the comment itself, so Carla doesn’t need to start another conversation.

• The document starts out private; you decide whether to share it.
  • Anyone who opens it needs a Claude account.
  • With "Anyone with the link," whoever has the link can open it, so share it only with people you trust. If the document uses Claude inside it or connects to your apps, this option isn’t available.

secoes.sub: All in claude.ai or the app. No terminal needed.

exercicios.texto: Ask for 7 slides based on one of your scripts, lessons, or texts, using Carla’s template. Make at least one change by typing a request. Then run the fact-check request.
exercicios.pronto: the presentation has 7 slides, you made 1 change by typing a request, and you noted 3 numbers, dates, or formulas checked against the original text.

exercicios.texto: Create a tracking document (guests, deliverables, or weekly tasks) using Carla’s adapted prompt, and share it with someone on your team using the Share button. Choose view, comment, or edit access. They’ll need to sign in with a Claude account to open it.
exercicios.pronto: you replaced the 3 EXAMPLE rows with 3 real livestreams (or tasks), checked the dates against your calendar, sent the link to someone on your team, and they opened it (working alone? you shared it and confirmed the share setting shows the access you chose, such as view).

exercicios.texto: In your document, leave a comment tagging @Claude with a request to review one row of the table. Only you, the document owner, can call on @Claude; the people you shared it with can view, comment, or edit, depending on the access you gave each one.
exercicios.pronto: Claude’s reply appears in the comment itself.

exercicios.texto: Dashboards is in beta (testing): if you don’t see it, skip this one. Get a simple spreadsheet with about 10 numbers (subscribers, sales, or expenses by month), and paste an adapted version of the "Numbers dashboard" prompt.
exercicios.pronto: the dashboard appears in the conversation and you checked 2 of its numbers against the spreadsheet.

exercicios.texto: Paste the "An image" prompt with what you want to promote. Make one change by typing a request (color, text size, or wording).
exercicios.pronto: the image appears in the conversation, you made 1 change by typing a request, and you read the text in the image without finding any errors.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Carla has a Pro plan and wants an animated video of the lesson. What does she find?
opcoes: Motion Studio, available on all plans.
Claude Motion, which exports MP4 on any paid plan.
Claude Motion is in beta for Team and Enterprise only; on Pro, she uses Slides and Design instead.
Claude Design, which turns any artwork into an animated video.
perguntas.explica: The official name is Claude Motion (“Motion Studio” doesn’t exist). It’s in beta and only available on Team and Enterprise plans. Slides and Design are available on all plans.

perguntas.p: Before sending a link to a numbers dashboard, what should you do?
opcoes: Check 3 numbers against the original source.
Ask Claude to rebuild the dashboard from scratch and compare it.
Change the colors to make it look more professional.
Send it and ask the recipient to let you know if they spot an error.
perguntas.explica: Claude can get a number wrong with complete confidence. Checking three numbers against the original spreadsheet catches most errors; if one is wrong, check them all.

perguntas.p: Who can tag @Claude in a document comment to have it review the document?
opcoes: Anyone with the link.
Only someone with a Team plan.
No one: Claude only reads the document when it’s created.
You, the document owner.
perguntas.explica: Recipients can view, comment, or edit, depending on their permissions. You, the doc owner, are the one who tags @Claude in the comments.

perguntas.p: A slide came out with tiny text. What’s the best request?
opcoes: “Redo the whole presentation. It’s bad.”
“Slide 5: make the text larger and use fewer words. Don’t change the others.”
Download the presentation and fix it in another program.
“Make all the slides prettier and more professional, please.”
perguntas.explica: Ask for specific changes in a few words, one at a time, and say where. Asking it to redo everything or make it “prettier” can ruin what was already right.

perguntas.p: Carla sent the guest document link to the moderator. What does the moderator need to open it?
opcoes: Nothing: the link opens for anyone, without an account.
A Team plan, because Pro isn’t enough.
Sign in with a Claude account.
Install the Claude app on her computer.
perguntas.explica: Anyone opening a Claude Docs document needs to sign in with a Claude account. Carla chooses whether the moderator can view, comment, or edit. A common mistake is assuming the link opens without an account.

itens.texto: Slides and Design on all plans; Dashboards in beta; Motion on Team and Enterprise only.
Compare 3 numbers or dates with the original source before sending the link.
View, comment, or edit; tag @Claude in comments on your document.
